6. We have discussed Eddington about his contribution to proving Einstein correct, one of the most dramatic stories (a bit closer home in a way) in science history is X’s conflict with Eddington, the foremost astrophysicist of the day. In 1935, X presented his findings at the Royal Astronomical Society. Immediately after his talk, Eddington stood up and publicly mocked the theory, calling it "absurd" and claiming there should be a law of nature to prevent stars from behaving that way. Because of Eddington’s massive influence, X’s work was largely ignored by the scientific community for decades. He eventually left England for the United States, feeling he had no future in British academia. He was finally proven correct nearly 40 years later. Id X.

1. X and Y (2008) is a BBC/HBO biographical drama that focuses on a pivotal but often overlooked partnership in scientific history. While X is the household name, the film highlights how his fame was cemented by the work of Y. The film is set against the backdrop of World War I, which adds a layer of high-stakes political tension to the scientific discovery. Y is tasked with proving X wrong to uphold British intellectual superiority, but instead, he finds himself convinced by X’s math. Id X, Y and what did Y do?
